scope: Complete four-page main, all five figures and 21-entry bibliography; SI and cited full papers unreviewed.

bibliographic_scope.title: Superparamagnetic Magnetite Colloidal Nanocrystal Clusters
bibliographic_scope.authors: Jianping Ge; Yongxing Hu; Maurizio Biasini; Ward P. Beyermann; Yadong Yin
bibliographic_scope.parallel_edition: 10.1002/ange.200700197; same study, no separate paper credit

stock.final_volume_and_molarity: Not reported; do not equate solvent volume to final stock volume.

common_precursor.PAA_molar_basis: Unspecified chain/repeat-unit basis; no molecular weight supplied

preparation_scope.post_injection: Heated a further 1 h; distinct hold setpoint and atmosphere continuation not separately specified.
preparation_scope.workup: Several washes with deionized water/ethanol mixture, then dispersion in deionized water; no separation method, volume, ratio or final concentration. Discussion separately states retained dispersibility after three washes.

structure_scope.morphology: Flowerlike three-dimensional clusters of primary crystals; source description with TEM.
structure_scope.TEM: Approximately 150 clusters measured for each average in Figure 1; all scale bars 200 nm; numerical distribution widths not tabulated.

31nm_HRTEM.interpretation: Similar orientation; oriented attachment/sintering explanation is author interpretation.

structure_scope.174nm_SAED: Single-crystal-like spots broadened into narrow arcs, interpreted as slight primary-crystal misalignment (Figure 2d). No extra distinct specimen or quantitative angular distribution.
structure_scope.XAS: The main refers to SI XAS to support magnetite composition. The SI is unreviewed; no XAS curve or fit result is invented.
structure_scope.coordinates: No atomic coordinates, refined cell, measured interface or unit-cell file supplied.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1–3 and structure discussion

magnetism.saturation_mass_basis: PAA-covered particle mass; polymer fraction is not specified.
magnetism.93nm_at_300K: No remanence or coercivity reported; source describes superparamagnetic behavior. Detection limit is not specified, so no exact zero with an invented error is assigned.

93nm_at_2K.Figure4ab_axis: −2000 to 2000 Oe; separate from the broader Figure 4c field cycle.

magnetism.Langevin_model: M(x)=Nμ[coth(x)−1/x], x=μH/(kBT); N is described as the number of clusters. The main presents fitted per-cluster moments; no refitting performed.

reference_8nm_nanodots.preparation: Not supplied in the scoped main; comparator only, no synthesis route or pair credit.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 and magnetic discussion

field_response.sample: CNC aqueous dispersion; exact cluster-size variant and concentration unspecified
field_response.Figure5abc: Dark-field optical images on glass before, during and after an applied field; chains form under field and disassemble after field removal. Bright corner regions are dried CNCs, not a second preparation.
field_response.Figure5def: Vial photographs without field, with field for 1 min, and after field removal. Authors describe complete magnetic separation within minutes and redispersion after slight agitation.
field_response.unknowns: Magnet geometry/field strength, concentration and size-specific sample identity are not given.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure 5, caption and text

source_interpretation.topic: Separate the cluster size from primary crystal size
source_interpretation.text: The authors assemble primary magnetite crystals into larger flowerlike clusters. TEM measures the overall cluster diameter, whereas HRTEM or Scherrer estimates describe the primary crystals. These sizes remain distinct: a 93 nm cluster has a reported 9.65 nm Scherrer grain size.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Cluster model, Figures 1–3

source_interpretation.text: The authors attribute the PAA choice to coordination of carboxylate groups with iron cations on magnetite. Uncoordinated carboxylate groups extending into water are proposed to provide dispersibility. Surface coverage, chain configuration and a unique polymer molecular graph are not measured.

The paper proposes that hot DEG/FeCl3/PAA with NaOH produces water and increases alkalinity, favoring hydrolysis. DEG is proposed to partly reduce Fe(OH)3 to Fe(OH)2, followed by dehydration to Fe3O4. Primary crystals then nucleate and aggregate into clusters; HRTEM alignment is interpreted as oriented attachment with subsequent high-temperature sintering. These are source interpretations, not directly isolated intermediate recipes.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Hydrolysis/growth discussion, Figure 2; cited references 3, 6, 19 and 20

source_interpretation.topic: Stock aliquot controls the reported cluster series
source_interpretation.text: Keeping the other stated method conditions fixed, the paper varies NaOH/DEG aliquot volume from 1.60 to 1.85 mL and reports six cluster diameters from 31 to 174 nm. The suggested explanation is a change in water concentration and alkalinity that affects FeCl3 hydrolysis. Neither pH nor water concentration is quantitatively measured in the main.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1, 4, Size-control discussion and Experimental Section

source_interpretation.topic: Magnetic response without a large single crystal
source_interpretation.text: The cluster series remains superparamagnetic at room temperature despite its larger overall size. The authors compare strong cluster magnetic response with an 8 nm reference nanodot, and propose that interactions among the primary crystals differ from those of a single crystal. The 93 nm sample has remanence and coercivity at 2 K. No measured critical size for every cluster or temperature-dependent phase change is inferred.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Magnetic discussion and Figure 4

source_interpretation.topic: Mass normalization and fitted moment have different meanings
source_interpretation.text: Saturation magnetization is reported per gram of PAA-covered particles. The paper suggests higher polymer mass fraction or surface disorder as possible reasons for lower small-particle values. Moment per cluster is separately obtained from a Langevin fit and is an author-derived result. The SI fit details and XAS data are not reviewed in this main-only contribution.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4c and adjacent discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Application outlook is distinct from demonstrated performance
source_interpretation.text: The authors propose uses in separation, targeted delivery and MRI, as well as future silica coating for ligand coupling. The main demonstrates field-induced chaining, magnetic separation and redispersion; it does not provide a biomedical validation, silica-shell synthesis or ligand-coupling recipe.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure 5 and outlook; reference 21
